newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans cool on govt but no friendlier to SPD - poll.
newsitem.headline: Germans cool on govt but no friendlier to SPD - poll.

text.p: German voters are grumbling more about Chancellor Helmut Kohl's government but still consider it better qualified than the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) to tackle economic problems, an opinion poll said on Friday.

ZDF television's monthly Politbarometer survey showed 53 percent of the 1,269 Germans polled said the centre-right government was doing badly. That was a rise of three percentage points over the October poll.
But only 20 percent -- one percent more than in October -- felt the SPD could do any better, said the survey carried out by the Election Research Group pollsters.
"Even though they are dissatisfied with the government, voters see a government led by (Kohl's) Christian Democrats as more competent in economics and finance than one led by the SPD," ZDF said.

It said 55 percent of SPD voters thought their party was still not well-run one year after the dynamic Saar state premier Oskar Lafontaine grabbed the chairman's job in a party congress coup from his faltering predecessor Rudolf Scharping.

The poll's survey of party popularity showed Kohl's coalition of Christian Democrats (CDU/CSU) and Free Democrats (FDP) scored 47 percent against 46 percent for a potential coalition of the SPD and ecologist Greens.
According to ZDF, 34 percent of those surveyed said the German economy was doing poorly and 58 percent said it was doing only "so-so." But 49 percent said they themselves were doing well financially.
To tackle Germany's budget problems, 79 percent supported further spending cuts, 66 percent wanted more state-owned firms privatised and only 11 percent were ready to accept higher taxes, ZDF said.
